threads.thread_goal: Align on program scope, targets, and pilot units before execution starts.

messages.text:
Kicking off the Cross-Unit Food Waste Reduction and Revenue Optimization Program for the next 30 days.

Objective is to reduce food waste across units while protecting margins and guest satisfaction. We will need a clear target, pilot units, and a simple way to track results.

I suggest we use the Food Waste Baseline and KPI Tracker (A1) as our main reference and connect it later with the Executive Dashboard Specification (A7).

For now, I would like us to focus on:
- defining the company-wide waste reduction target and timeline (T1)
- mapping current waste-related processes in a few pilot units (T2)
- preparing to enroll units into the pilot (T8) using the Pilot Unit Readiness Checklist (A8)

@department manager and @sales manager, can you share which units you think are best suited as pilots and what a realistic reduction target could be within 6 months, given the constraints on costs and guest satisfaction?

Thanks for starting this.

From an operations view, I would propose we start with three units where managers are already used to tracking KPIs in some form, so they can adapt more easily to A1 and A8.

My first thought for pilots:
- City Center Bistro
- Riverside Grill
- Airport Express

They have different patterns (lunch-heavy, dinner-heavy, high turnover), which should give us a good spread for T2 and later T8.

On the reduction target, I need a bit more clarity on our current baseline. Do we already have any consolidated waste percentage in A1, or do we need to collect that first before we commit to a number for T1?

On pilots, I agree with focusing on units that already have some discipline around numbers.

I like the three units that were just mentioned. They also have different menu mixes, which will help later when we design the menu and sales playbook (A4) and training (A5).

On the target: in similar programs I have seen, a 10–15 percent reduction in measured waste over 6 months is usually achievable without hurting guest satisfaction, as long as we do not cut portions blindly.

Given our 30-day design and pilot window, I would suggest:
- first 2 weeks: collect baseline in the three pilot units using A1
- next 2 weeks: start applying new routines and see if we can already move the needle a bit

We could tentatively aim for 12 percent reduction in those pilots over 6 months, and then adjust once we see the first data. But I would like to hear from both of you if that feels realistic for T1.

Jumping in to make sure we stay aligned with the 30-day deadline and the constraints.

On the target: I like the idea of a clear percentage and a 6-month horizon, but I want to be sure we can measure it properly with A1 and that it does not create pressure that leads to stock-outs or guest complaints.

Could we define the target in two steps for T1:
- a provisional company-wide target now, based on what @sales manager suggested
- a formal confirmation after the first two weeks of pilot data, when we review A1 and A7 together

If that works, I would lean toward 10 percent as the initial company-wide target over 6 months, with the pilots aiming for 12 percent as a stretch. Does that sound acceptable from an operations standpoint?

I like the two-step approach.

Given what you all shared, I propose we confirm:
- company-wide target: 10 percent reduction in measured food waste over 6 months
- pilot stretch target: 12 percent reduction over the same period
- first 2 weeks of the 30-day window focused on establishing a baseline in the three pilot units using A1

If there are no strong objections, I will treat this as our agreed target for T1 and we can document it in the target document and in A7.

Please react with a thumbs up if you are ok with this, or comment if you see a major risk.

Thumbs up from my side.

From a sales and guest experience angle, a 10 percent reduction over 6 months is reasonable as long as we:
- avoid cutting signature items without testing
- use menu engineering and promotions to steer demand rather than just cutting orders

We can build these principles into the playbook (A4) and the staff training deck (A5) later.

On pilots, I support the three units listed earlier. They give us enough variety to test different sales tactics during T8.

Works for me as well.

On the pilot units: City Center Bistro, Riverside Grill, and Airport Express are confirmed from my side. I will start mapping current waste-related processes there for T2.

One concern: staff capacity to handle new tracking routines. To reduce resistance, I suggest we keep the first version of the process very light and align it with existing checks. We can use A8 to make sure each unit is ready before we start T8.

I will need some support from the unit managers to gather the baseline data into A1. I will coordinate that directly with them.

From a purchasing side, the three proposed pilot units are also good candidates. They have enough volume that changes in ordering patterns will show up clearly in A1.

Once T2 gives us a clearer view of where waste is happening, I can start on T4 and T5 for those units, making sure we respect existing supplier contracts and avoid stock-outs.

For the timeline: if we start baseline tracking in week 1, I can have a first pass on high-waste categories and potential purchasing adjustments ready before the end of week 2, so it feeds into the pilot start for T8.

On the pilot start date, to keep the 30-day window realistic, I suggest:
- Week 1: finalize T1 and start T2 in the three pilot units
- Week 2: complete baseline entries in A1 and review them together
- Start of Week 3: official pilot start date for T8, assuming A8 is green for all three units

If we agree on this, we can set the pilot start date as the Monday of Week 3. That gives us two full weeks of pilot activity within the 30 days.

Any objections to using that Monday as the formal pilot start date for T8?

No objection from me.

Let us confirm:
- Pilot units: City Center Bistro, Riverside Grill, Airport Express
- Pilot start date: Monday of Week 3 in our 30-day window, provided A8 is complete for each unit

We will treat the first two weeks as baseline and preparation, then switch to the new routines from that Monday.

I will document this in the program overview and link it to T8 and A8.

Unless someone flags a major issue today, we will consider this decision closed.

The Monday of Week 3 works for sales and training planning.

I will start sketching how we can brief the teams in those three units ahead of that date, so they understand why we are tracking waste and how it links to sales behaviors.

Once T7 is underway, we can align the training content with the targets in T1 and the pilot plan in T8.

All clear.

I will:
- confirm with the three unit managers that they can support T2 starting this week
- use A8 to check readiness (staff briefed, simple tracking sheets printed, basic process explained)
- start filling A1 with whatever baseline data we already have, then refine as we go

I will post a short update at the end of the week with where we stand on T2 and readiness for T8.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalize the waste tracking process and supporting tools.

messages.text:
Sharing the first draft of the waste tracking template and routine for feedback.

I have created a simple version of the Food Waste Baseline and KPI Tracker (A1) tailored for daily use in the three pilot units, and a short Standard Operating Procedure for Food Waste Tracking (A2).

Key points:
- Daily sheet: records item, quantity wasted, reason (prep error, overproduction, expired, plate waste), and estimated cost
- Weekly summary: auto-calculates total waste cost and percentage vs food cost
- Routine: kitchen lead fills in the sheet at end of each shift; manager reviews weekly and logs into A1

This is linked to T3 and will also feed into the staff training materials for T7.

I would appreciate your comments on:
- is the level of detail manageable for staff?
- which KPIs from A1 should be visible in the executive dashboard (A7) for T9?

Please share any changes you think are needed before we test this in one pilot unit for three days, as required by T3.

Thanks for putting this together.

On the template:
- The daily sheet structure looks good. I would add a simple category field (protein, veg, starch, dessert, other) so we can quickly see where the biggest issues are.
- For reasons, maybe we can pre-define a short list with codes to speed up entry and reduce free text.

On KPIs for A7 and T9, I suggest we start with:
- waste cost as a percentage of food cost per unit
- waste per cover (in cost)
- top 5 items by waste cost

These are easy to explain to managers and will help us later when we design the menu and sales playbook (A4).

From a purchasing perspective, the template is a good start.

To make T4 easier later, I would like to see:
- a link between each waste line and the supplier or at least the product group
- a flag for items that were over-ordered vs items that were produced but not sold

This will help us identify high-waste categories and adjust order frequency and minimum order quantities in line with A3.

For the executive dashboard (A7), I would also recommend a simple view of waste by product group, so we can see if changes in purchasing are having the expected effect.

Looking at this with the dashboard in mind.

For A7 and T9, I would like the following KPIs to be available at least weekly:
- waste cost percentage vs food cost, by unit and overall
- trend over time (even if we only have a few weeks at first)
- top waste reasons (overproduction, prep error, expiry, plate waste)

We should keep the number of KPIs small at the beginning so that unit managers do not feel overwhelmed.

On the routine: do you think managers will have enough time to review weekly and log into A1, or should we consider a bi-weekly review at first to reduce the load?

I like the suggestions so far.

On the review cadence, my concern is that if we go bi-weekly, we might react too slowly during the pilot. Weekly feels like a good compromise, but we need to keep the process simple.

Maybe we can:
- keep the daily entries very light, as in the draft
- have a short weekly review (15 minutes) where the manager looks at the summary and notes one or two actions

If we agree on this, we can lock in the weekly reporting cadence for T3 and T9 and reflect it in A2 and A7.

Weekly review is manageable if we keep the template tight.

I will update A2 and the template to include:
- category field (protein, veg, starch, dessert, other)
- short list of reason codes
- product group field that we can later map to suppliers for T4

For the executive dashboard (A7), I will structure the data in A1 so that we can show:
- waste cost percentage vs food cost
- waste per cover
- top 5 items by waste cost
- waste by product group

Unless there are objections, I will treat this as the agreed set of KPIs for T9 and A7.

No objections from me.

For T7, I will make sure the training materials explain the reason codes and categories clearly, with examples from kitchen, service, and sales.

One small suggestion: in the daily sheet, can we add a simple field for whether the waste was avoidable or unavoidable? That will help us focus on the right actions in the units.

Agree on the avoidable vs unavoidable field. It will also help us when we talk to suppliers and adjust purchasing rules in A3.

If we see a lot of avoidable waste linked to over-ordering, that is a clear signal for T4. If it is mostly unavoidable (like trimming), we might need to look at product specs instead.

With the KPIs and fields you described, I am comfortable that A1 will give us enough information for the executive dashboard (A7) and for our monthly review cadence.

For T9, I would like to see a first mock-up of the dashboard views once we have at least one week of pilot data. That will help us check if the data structure is working as expected.

Before we move ahead, I want to be sure we are all aligned that this template and routine will be our standard for the pilot.

To summarize the current version:
- daily entries with item, quantity, category, reason code, avoidable vs unavoidable, product group
- weekly summary with waste cost percentage vs food cost, waste per cover, top 5 items by waste cost, waste by product group
- weekly manager review and logging into A1

If everyone is ok, we will:
- approve this as the standard waste tracking template and reporting cadence for the pilot (T3)
- test it in one pilot unit for three days starting early next week, then roll out to the other two pilot units if no major issues appear

Please react or comment today so we can close this and move on.

I am aligned with this version and the weekly cadence.

From the units side, the key will be to keep the daily routine simple and to show managers quickly how the data will be used in A7, so it does not feel like extra admin work.

I will reflect the final template and routine in the training deck (A5) and quick reference guide for T7.

Count me in as well.

Once the three-day test is done in the first pilot unit, I would like to review the data briefly to see if we can already spot any obvious high-waste categories. That will help me prioritize work on T4 and T5.

Given the feedback and the reactions, I will treat the current template and weekly cadence as approved for the pilot.

Next steps on my side for T3:
- finalize the template and SOP in A2 by tomorrow
- brief the manager and kitchen lead in one pilot unit
- run the three-day test and capture any issues

If no major problems appear, we will roll out the same routine to the other two pilot units as part of T8.

threads.thread_goal: Align purchasing rules and supplier arrangements with waste targets.

messages.text:
Sharing initial analysis of high-waste categories and proposed purchasing changes for the three pilot units.

Using the early entries in A1 and the process maps from T2, I have identified the following high-waste categories:
- fresh herbs and salad greens
- bakery items (bread and pastries)
- pre-cut fruit

Key drivers seem to be over-ordering for weekends and unpredictable demand.

My proposal for T4, to be captured in the Purchasing and Inventory Adjustment Guidelines (A3):
1) Fresh herbs and salad greens
- reduce order quantities by 15 percent for weekdays
- increase order frequency from twice to three times per week where suppliers allow
2) Bakery items
- shift part of the volume to a supplier that offers smaller batch deliveries (see A6)
- introduce a standing rule to freeze surplus bread at end of day where food safety allows
3) Pre-cut fruit
- tighten par levels based on last 4 weeks of sales
- introduce a rule to only order pre-cut for weekends and use whole fruit during weekdays

For T5, I have also drafted a list of top 5 suppliers for perishable goods in A6, with notes on which ones already offer flexible quantities or schedules.

I would like your feedback on:
- any operational risks you see with these changes
- which suppliers we should prioritize for more flexible delivery terms.

Thanks for the breakdown.

From the units side, a few points:
- Increasing delivery frequency for greens is helpful, but we need to check storage capacity in Airport Express. They are tight on space.
- Freezing surplus bread is possible in City Center Bistro and Riverside Grill, but we need clear guidance on what is acceptable from a food safety perspective.
- Switching pre-cut fruit to whole fruit on weekdays might require some extra prep time in the kitchen.

I do not see major blockers, but we should pilot these changes in just one unit first before applying them to all three, to avoid stock-outs or quality issues.

On the sales and guest side:
- For bakery items, we need to be careful that freezing does not affect quality for breakfast guests. Maybe we can limit frozen bread to toast and keep fresh for premium items.
- For pre-cut fruit, guests at Airport Express expect speed. Using whole fruit on weekdays might slow service unless we adjust prep routines.

I suggest we:
- test the bakery and fruit changes first in Riverside Grill, where service pressure is a bit lower
- monitor guest feedback and waste data in A1 closely during the first two weeks.

From a risk perspective, I want to make sure we do not breach any existing supplier contracts and that we stay within food safety rules.

On A6, do we have clarity on minimum order quantities and delivery frequency clauses for the current suppliers? If not, we should double-check before we commit to changes in T4.

For T5, I would prioritize suppliers where:
- we already have a good relationship
- they have some flexibility in their logistics

Can you suggest which two or three suppliers from the top 5 in A6 we should approach first?

On A6, I have checked the contracts for the top 5 perishable suppliers.

Summary:
- Supplier 1 (greens and herbs): minimum order quantity is moderate, but they already deliver three times per week to some units. They are a good candidate for more flexible quantities.
- Supplier 2 (bakery): fixed daily delivery, but they can adjust volumes with 24 hours notice.
- Supplier 3 (fruit): offers both whole and pre-cut, with some flexibility on product mix.

For T5, I recommend we prioritize:
- Supplier 1 and Supplier 3 for flexible quantities and product mix
- Supplier 2 as a secondary focus for adjusting bakery volumes

On the operational side, I agree with testing the bakery and fruit changes first in Riverside Grill, as suggested, and starting with greens adjustments in City Center Bistro where storage is less of an issue.

Thanks for the detailed work.

To keep things safe during the pilot, I propose we:
- apply the full set of purchasing changes (greens, bakery, pre-cut fruit) only in Riverside Grill for the first two weeks
- apply only the greens adjustments in City Center Bistro at first
- keep Airport Express on current rules until we see the first results

This way, we can monitor A1 and avoid surprises in the most time-sensitive unit.

If we agree, we can treat these as the revised purchasing rules for the pilot units under T4, documented in A3.

This phased approach works for operations.

I will coordinate with the managers in Riverside Grill and City Center Bistro to:
- adjust par levels and ordering patterns according to A3
- brief kitchen teams on the new rules and how they link to the waste tracking in A1

We will keep Airport Express as a control unit for now.

Aligned from my side.

For Riverside Grill, I will work with the manager to adjust menu and display slightly so that we do not over-push items that might be constrained by the new purchasing rules.

We will also keep an eye on guest feedback, especially around breakfast bakery and fruit offers.

On supplier prioritization, I agree with focusing on Supplier 1 and Supplier 3 first, then Supplier 2.

For T5, please go ahead and schedule meetings with Supplier 1 and Supplier 3 this week, and capture notes in A6.

We should aim to secure at least some flexibility on quantities and delivery days for the pilot units, without changing overall contract terms.

Given the feedback, I will:
- update A3 to reflect the phased purchasing rules you described
- treat Riverside Grill as the full test unit and City Center Bistro as partial test for greens
- keep Airport Express unchanged for now

Unless there are objections today, we can consider these revised purchasing rules approved for the pilot under T4.

No objections from me.

Let us confirm:
- Revised purchasing rules for the pilot units are as described in the updated A3
- Riverside Grill: full set of changes
- City Center Bistro: greens adjustments only
- Airport Express: no changes during the first phase

We will monitor A1 closely and adjust if we see stock-outs or quality issues.

I will mark these purchasing rules as approved for T4.

Understood.

I will prioritize Supplier 1 and Supplier 3 for T5 and log all meeting notes and any agreed flexibilities in A6.

Goal is to secure at least:
- smaller batch sizes for greens and herbs
- flexibility to switch between whole and pre-cut fruit for the pilot units

I will share a short summary once the meetings are done.

Thanks. Once you have the outcomes from Supplier 1 and Supplier 3, we can decide whether it is worth approaching Supplier 2 during this pilot phase or wait until we have more data from A1.

For now, let us treat Supplier 1 and Supplier 3 as our priority suppliers for flexible delivery terms under T5.

threads.thread_goal: Define menu, sales tactics, and communication plan for the pilot.

messages.text:
Sharing draft menu recommendations and sales playbook for the pilot units.

Based on early waste data in A1 and input from unit managers, I have prepared a first version of the Menu and Sales Playbook for Low-Waste Items (A4) and a draft of the staff training deck (A5).

For T6, the proposed list of low-waste, high-margin priority items includes:
- Roast chicken bowl with seasonal veg
- Pasta of the day using surplus veg
- Chef salad with flexible toppings
- Breakfast combo with toast and whole fruit

Key sales tactics in A4:
- highlight these items on menus and boards with a small icon
- upsell scripts for servers to suggest these items when guests are undecided
- limited-time offers to test guest response without locking in permanent changes

For T10, I have also drafted an internal announcement explaining the program and how it links to our targets in T1.

I would like your feedback on:
- the final list of priority items for the pilot
- any concerns about guest perception or operational complexity
- how we should adjust sales incentives later under T12.

Thanks for the draft.

From an operations view:
- The roast chicken bowl and pasta of the day are easy to execute and flexible for using surplus veg.
- The chef salad is fine, but we need to be careful not to increase waste of toppings if demand is lower than expected.
- The breakfast combo with toast and whole fruit fits well with the purchasing changes we are testing in Riverside Grill.

I would suggest we add one more hot vegetarian option to the priority list, to give servers more variety when recommending items.

From the purchasing side, the proposed items align well with the categories we are trying to manage.

The roast chicken bowl and pasta of the day will help us use surplus veg and reduce waste in the greens and veg categories.

For the breakfast combo, we should make sure the bread and fruit options match the flexibility we are negotiating with Supplier 1 and Supplier 3 in A6.

I support adding a vegetarian hot dish that uses similar ingredients, so we do not create new low-rotation items.

On communication (T10), I like that the internal announcement links the program to our overall targets and to guest satisfaction.

One request: can we include a short section explaining that the priority items are chosen because they are both guest-friendly and help us reduce waste? That will help staff explain it positively to guests.

On incentives (T12), I would be cautious about changing the scheme too quickly. Maybe we can start with a small recognition for units that hit both sales and waste targets during the pilot, and only later adjust formal incentives.

The proposed items look good to me, but I want to be sure we are not overcomplicating the menu for the pilot units.

Could we:
- limit the priority list to 4–5 items per unit
- ensure that at least 3 of them are common across all three pilot units, so we can compare results in A1 more easily

If we can agree on a final list that meets these criteria, we can treat it as the official pilot list for T6.

Makes sense.

Proposal for the final pilot list:
Common across all three units:
- Roast chicken bowl with seasonal veg
- Pasta of the day using surplus veg
- Chef salad with flexible toppings
- Breakfast combo with toast and whole fruit

Plus one unit-specific vegetarian hot dish in each unit, using similar ingredients:
- City Center Bistro: Veggie grain bowl
- Riverside Grill: Roasted veg flatbread
- Airport Express: Veggie breakfast wrap

That gives us 5 priority items per unit, with 4 common across all three.

If everyone is comfortable with this, we can lock it in for T6 and A4.

This list works operationally.

The unit-specific vegetarian options can be built from ingredients we already use, so they should not create extra complexity.

We will need to brief kitchen and service teams clearly, which we can cover in A5 and during T7.

Aligned from purchasing.

I will make sure the par levels and ordering rules in A3 reflect these priority items, so we do not run out of key ingredients during the pilot.

Given the feedback, I am comfortable confirming this as the pilot list of priority low-waste items.

We will:
- use the 4 common items across all three pilot units
- add one vegetarian hot dish per unit as described

I will note this in the program overview and link it to T6 and A4.

On communication and incentives:

For T10, I will update the internal announcement to include a short explanation that the priority items are both guest favorites and help us reduce waste. I will also add a simple FAQ section for common guest questions.

For T12, I suggest we start with:
- a small recognition (for example, a mention in the weekly update) for units that hit both sales and waste targets during the pilot
- a simple scorecard in A1 or a related sheet showing sales mix of priority items and waste metrics

We can then use the pilot results to design a more formal incentive adjustment later, once we see what behaviors actually move the numbers.

That approach works for me.

For T10, once you have the updated internal announcement and the optional external messaging outline, please share them so we can sign off.

On T12, I agree that we should treat the pilot as a learning phase and avoid major changes to the formal incentive scheme until we have at least one full cycle of data.

To close the loop on communication and incentives for the pilot:

I propose we agree that, during the pilot phase:
- internal communication will focus on explaining the why, the priority items, and how staff can contribute (T10)
- recognition will be informal (mentions in updates, simple scorecards) rather than changes to the formal incentive scheme (T12)

If everyone is aligned, we can treat this as our approach for the pilot, and revisit formal incentive adjustments after we review the pilot results.

Aligned.

I will finalize:
- the menu and sales playbook (A4) with the agreed priority items
- the training deck (A5) including upsell scripts and the communication points we discussed
- the internal announcement and external messaging outline for T10

We can then use the pilot to test how well the recognition and scorecards drive behavior before proposing any formal incentive changes under T12.

threads.thread_goal: Review early pilot results and decide on adjustments or scale-up.

messages.text:
Sharing first consolidated pilot results from the baseline tracker.

We have completed two weeks of pilot activity in the three units, with the tracking template in A1 and the routines defined in A2.

Headline numbers:
- Overall waste cost percentage vs food cost: down from 6.5 percent baseline to 5.7 percent across the three units
- Riverside Grill: from 7.0 percent to 5.6 percent
- City Center Bistro: from 6.0 percent to 5.5 percent
- Airport Express (control): stable at around 6.4 percent

We also have a first draft of the executive dashboard views in A7, based on T9.

Key observations:
- Biggest reductions came from greens and bakery in Riverside Grill, where we applied the full purchasing changes from A3 and the menu tactics from A4.
- Plate waste is still high for a few non-priority items.

For T11, I have started a short report summarizing these insights and some initial recommendations.

I would like your input on:
- whether we should adjust our overall targets in T1 based on these early results
- whether the dashboard views in A7 are sufficient for a broader rollout
- if we are ready to scale some of the changes to Airport Express or additional units.

These early results are encouraging.

From a sales and guest perspective:
- Priority items from A4 are selling well in Riverside Grill and City Center Bistro, with no negative trend in guest satisfaction scores.
- In Airport Express, where we did not change purchasing or menu focus, waste and sales mix look similar to baseline.

I would not change the overall 10 percent target in T1 yet, but this suggests we are on the right track.

On the dashboard (A7), the current views on waste percentage, waste per cover, and top waste items are already useful. I would add a simple view of sales mix of priority items vs others, so we can see how sales behaviors are contributing.

From the purchasing side, the data confirms that the adjustments in A3 are working, especially for greens and bakery in Riverside Grill.

We have not seen stock-outs, and quality complaints are minimal.

I would recommend:
- extending the greens adjustments to Airport Express
- starting a lighter version of the bakery changes there as well, while monitoring A1 closely

I do not think we need to change the overall target in T1 yet, but these results suggest that the 10 percent reduction over 6 months is achievable if we scale carefully.

Looking at the numbers, the trend is positive but still early.

On T1, I would prefer to keep the 10 percent target as is for now and revisit after another month of data. We can treat these results as confirmation that we do not need to lower the target.

On A7, I like the current views and agree with adding a sales mix view as suggested. That will help us see the link between menu tactics and waste reduction.

For scale-up, I am comfortable with extending some of the purchasing and menu changes to Airport Express, as long as we monitor guest satisfaction and service speed closely.

I agree that it is too early to change the overall target.

Given the early success, I suggest we:
- reconfirm the 10 percent company-wide target and 12 percent pilot stretch target in T1
- use the next month to validate that the trend continues before considering any adjustments

On the dashboard (A7), let us add the sales mix view and keep the rest as is for now.

If there are no objections, we will treat this as our decision on targets and dashboard views for the next phase.

Works for me.

For T11, I will finalize the short report with:
- summary of the waste and revenue metrics from A1
- what worked well (purchasing changes, menu focus, tracking routine)
- issues to watch (plate waste on a few non-priority items)
- recommendations for scale-up to Airport Express and potentially one more unit

I will also coordinate with the Airport Express manager to prepare for extending the greens and bakery changes and the priority items from A4.

On scale-up to Airport Express:
- We should introduce the priority items from A4 gradually, starting with the breakfast combo and the veggie breakfast wrap, which fit the guest profile there.
- We will need to pay attention to service speed, so I will work with the manager to adjust prep routines.

I will also use the training materials in A5 to brief the team, focusing on how their sales behaviors link to the waste metrics in A1.

I will prepare a simple plan to extend the greens and bakery purchasing rules from A3 to Airport Express, with slightly more conservative reductions at first.

We will monitor A1 weekly for any signs of stock-outs or quality issues and adjust quickly if needed.

These changes will be included in the recommendations section of the T11 report.

On the dashboard views in A7, once the sales mix view is added, I think we are in a good position to use this as the standard for leadership reporting.

For T9, I would like to schedule a short review with the leadership team next week to walk through the dashboard and the T11 report, and confirm that the views meet their needs before we roll out to more units.

To summarize where we stand after these first pilot results:
- We are keeping the 10 percent company-wide target and 12 percent pilot stretch target in T1, based on the positive early trend.
- The executive dashboard views in A7, with the added sales mix view, will be our standard for the next phase.
- We will extend the successful purchasing and menu changes to Airport Express, with careful monitoring.

Next steps will be to finalize the T11 report, adjust A7 accordingly, and prepare a proposal for scaling to additional units after the leadership review.
